rule: A relative deadline resolves against the meeting's date: "end of (the) week" is the Friday of the meeting's week. A genuinely ambiguous date stays unresolved (due null). Only a date said for finishing the work is its deadline; a date for starting or resuming it is not.

A concrete deliverable inside a broader work item is recorded on that item by default (a checklist entry on the story, a note on the task), keeping its specific action and deliverable in words, never a vague summary. It is a separate linked task only when its own owner or its own deadline is stated explicitly. It decomposes related work; it never merges unrelated actions.

A routine reminder or chase is attached to the work it chases, not a new item. It is its own task only for a substantive escalation or an independently accountable follow-up, owned by whoever follows up, never copied from the deliverable's owner. When the chased work cannot be identified, its linkage is unresolved; never a guessed match.

A continuing change to how the team works is a decision when the transcript supports adoption. A one-off logistical action is evaluated under the existing logistics rule. A suggestion alone is not an adopted decision.
Concrete preparation or investigation counts as work when its expected outcome is stated; DELIVERABLE-IN-PARENT decides its representation. A vague intent to discuss or think is not a committed task.

Commitment, responsible party and execution status are separate fields for client work as for ours: work the client explicitly undertook is committed, its responsible party is the client (client_owner, client_owed true), and its status says whether it is under way.

Contributors are not accountable ownership: work two people say they are doing together records both as contributors, and an owner only when one is named as accountable; otherwise the owner stays unresolved.
